subject: biology
topic: Variation and heredity: Mendelian genetics, crosses and ratios

kept.q: In tomato plants, tallness (T) is dominant over dwarfness (t). A tall tomato plant of unknown genotype was crossed with a dwarf plant, and the offspring were 48 tall and 52 dwarf plants. What is the genotype of the tall parent?
kept.explanation: A ratio close to 1 tall to 1 dwarf shows a test cross result. This only happens when the tall parent is heterozygous (Tt) crossed with tt.
kept.pidgin: If you get about 1 tall to 1 dwarf for your pikin them, na test cross be that. E mean say the tall papa or mama na Tt, wey you cross with tt.

kept.q: Which of the following best explains why a cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt x Tt) produces offspring in the ratio of 3 tall to 1 dwarf?
options: The dwarf allele is lost during fertilisation
Tallness and dwarfness blend to form intermediate plants
Three out of four possible allele combinations contain at least one dominant allele
The dominant allele doubles its effect in the heterozygous condition
kept.explanation: The possible combinations from Tt x Tt are TT, Tt, Tt and tt. Three of these four combinations carry at least one dominant T allele, giving tall plants, while only tt is dwarf.
kept.pidgin: Na TT, Tt, Tt and tt you go get when you cross Tt and Tt. Three out of these four join-join get at least one dominant T allele, na why you get 3 tall to 1 dwarf.

kept.q: A Nigerian farmer crosses a pure-breeding black-feathered chicken with a pure-breeding white-feathered chicken, and all the offspring have grey feathers, a colour between black and white. What type of gene action best explains this result?
kept.explanation: When the heterozygous offspring show a blended phenotype that is intermediate between both parents, this is called incomplete dominance. Neither allele completely masks the other.
kept.pidgin: If black and white mating produce grey wey dey middle, na incomplete dominance be that. None of the allele fit cover the other one fully, so dem blend together.

kept.q: In a dihybrid cross between two pea plants heterozygous for seed colour and seed texture (YyRr x YyRr), what fraction of the offspring is expected to be homozygous recessive for both traits?
kept.explanation: A dihybrid cross gives a 9:3:3:1 ratio out of 16 total offspring. The genotype yyrr, which is homozygous recessive for both traits, makes up only 1 part out of the 16.
kept.pidgin: For dihybrid cross, the last one for 9:3:3:1 ratio na yyrr. E dey represent only 1 part out of the 16 total offspring.

kept.q: A plant breeder wants to find out whether a tall pea plant showing the dominant phenotype is homozygous (TT) or heterozygous (Tt). Which cross would best help the breeder determine this?
options: Cross the tall plant with another tall plant of unknown genotype
Cross the tall plant with a homozygous recessive dwarf plant
Self-pollinate the tall plant and observe the F1 generation only
Cross the tall plant with a heterozygous tall plant
kept.explanation: Crossing an organism of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive individual is called a test cross. If any offspring show the recessive trait, the unknown parent must be heterozygous.
kept.pidgin: To know whether plant na TT or Tt, you must cross am with recessive dwarf tt. If any dwarf pikin show face, you don know say na Tt.

kept.q: A pure-breeding round-seeded pea plant (RR) is crossed with a pure-breeding wrinkled-seeded pea plant (rr). What are the expected genotype and phenotype of the F1 offspring?
kept.explanation: Crossing RR with rr gives only Rr offspring in the F1 generation. Since round seed shape is dominant, all the F1 plants show round seeds.
kept.pidgin: When you cross RR and rr, all the F1 pikin go carry Rr genotype. Because round seed dey dominant, everywhere go round.

q.q: Who is widely regarded as the father of modern genetics, having carried out breeding experiments on garden pea plants that led to the laws of inheritance?
q.explanation: Gregor Mendel performed experiments with pea plants in the 19th century and formulated the basic laws of inheritance. He is therefore called the father of genetics.

q.q: In sickle cell inheritance, the allele for normal haemoglobin (Hb^A) and the allele for sickle haemoglobin (Hb^S) show codominance, so heterozygotes (Hb^A Hb^S) produce both normal and sickle-shaped red blood cells. If two people with sickle cell trait (Hb^A Hb^S) marry, what proportion of their children is expected to have sickle cell anaemia (Hb^S Hb^S)?
q.explanation: Crossing Hb^A Hb^S with Hb^A Hb^S gives genotypes in the ratio 1 Hb^A Hb^A : 2 Hb^A Hb^S : 1 Hb^S Hb^S. Only one out of four offspring is expected to be Hb^S Hb^S, which causes sickle cell anaemia.
